receipts.by: builder lane C (claude subagent), for Vandor's review
receipts.what: Every preset on a 10 s synthetic excerpt (1280x720p60 + 3 Opus tracks, or 640x360p30 ffv1 with a moving soft alpha): youtube_4k60, youtube_4k60_fast and shorts land at -14.0 LUFS / -1.7 dBTP (target -14 / -1.5) with exactly 600 frames; proxy_edit and mezzanine_dnxhr keep all three tracks with their names; alpha_webm (VP9 alpha_mode 1), alpha_prores4444 (yuva444p12le) and alpha_webp_anim keep graded alpha with exactly 300 frames. alpha_webp_anim through Pillow: alpha error 0 on all 300 frames; the same clip through ffmpeg's libwebp: 66 at frame 1, 249 at frame 30.
receipts.how: ARSENAL_MEDIA_SLOW=1 py -m pytest tests/test_arsenal_media_export.py -q (about 70 s; 21 s without the 4K presets and the 10 s WebP)

receipts.by: builder lane C (claude subagent), for Vandor's review
receipts.what: shorts_1080x1920 on 10 s of 2026-10-11 17-51-11 (1590-1600 s): -41.2 LUFS in, -14.1 LUFS / -1.6 dBTP out in 5.5 s; the first AAC render read back at -1.4 dBTP (over -1.5, the studio's old miss) and the re-render with the overshoot subtracted fixed it. proxy_edit on the same range: 600 frames in 1.9 s.

notes: arsenal/media/export.py: presets from arsenal/media/presets.json (promoted from the studio's export_presets.json; alpha_webp_anim encoded with Pillow). Audio is rendered first (mix of the chosen tracks, measured two-pass loudnorm read back after the final codec, one corrective re-render) and stream-copied into the single video encode; qc checks frames, duration to one frame, loudness and true peak, track names and alpha. AMF encodes of ranges over 30 s hold the house GPU lock. Pillow (HPND) encodes the WebP. The ffmpeg that arsenal.media.ff locates is a separate process whose licence depends on the build; the one saved on this machine is configured --enable-gpl --enable-version3, so it is not asserted here.
